ownership_decision.invariant: Operations owns platform agent registrations, the global agent brake and agent runs; a run takes a step only while its agent is enabled and the brake is released.

boundary_decision.interaction: Operations imports no other context. The operator's identity reaches its handler through a function the composition root injects; the worker registers the agents defined in code at start.

domain_forces: Agents that act for the platform need an off switch that holds between one step and the next, not only at the start of a run.
An agent's tools and actions are Go registries, so what an agent may do cannot be widened by editing a row.
implementation_design.decision: Agent definitions live in code and are mirrored into the database at worker start, disabled until an operator enables them; the brake is a single row that exists only while engaged; every step first reads the agent and the brake and ends the run as stopped when either says so.
invariants_preserved: Identity owns accounts and the operator roster.
Audit events are written in the same transaction as the change they record.
rejected_alternatives: Agents defined only in the database: a row could name tools and actions the code does not have.
Checking the switch only when a run starts: a disable would wait for the run to finish.

record.name: Operations
record.responsibility: Owns the platform's own agents: who each one is, whether it may run, the brake that stops them all, and the record of every run.

approvals.scope: Operations as a new supporting context owning platform agent registrations, the global agent brake and agent runs, importing no other context
